name: Sheesham Wood 6-Seater Dining Set
short_description: Solid Indian rosewood from Jodhpur, kiln dried to 8–12%. Knock-down flat pack on ISPM-15 pallets, 60–70 sets in a 40ft HQ, 45–60 day lead time.
long_description: Sheesham — Indian rosewood, Dalbergia sissoo — is the timber Jodhpur built its furniture trade on. It is dense, takes a matte lacquer without blotching, and shows dark grain streaks against a warm mid-brown ground that buyers recognise on sight. A six-seater set is one table and six chairs, built as a matched lot from the same timber batch so the colour reads as one piece of furniture rather than seven.

Moisture content is the whole game on wooden furniture export. We kiln dry to 8–12% and hold it there, because a set built at Indian ambient humidity and shipped to a heated house in Germany or a dry winter in Chicago will split at the joints within a season. The moisture reading is taken at packing and recorded on the packing list.

Sets ship knock-down as flat pack, which roughly doubles what fits in a container and cuts transit damage close to nil. Assembly needs one Allen key and no glue. Natural, walnut and distressed matte finishes are standard; custom dimensions and buyer finishes are accepted from one container.

name: Reclaimed Wood Sideboard
short_description: Recycled hardwood on an iron frame, multi-tone or natural. Shipped assembled on ISPM-15 pallets, 90–110 units in a 40ft HQ. Lead with the sustainability story.
long_description: This piece is built from reclaimed hardwood — old doors, beams and shutters pulled from buildings across Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, cut down, planed and rebuilt into panelled fronts on a black iron frame. No two units are identical, and that is the product, not a defect: buyers who want uniform should be looking at the mango wood range instead.

The sustainability angle here is real and worth leading with in your own marketing. The timber is genuinely recovered rather than newly felled, the finishes are low-VOC, and the iron is locally fabricated. Retailers in the USA and Northern Europe increasingly ask for a substantiated claim rather than a word on a swing tag, and we can supply the recovered-timber declaration to back it.

Because the panels are reclaimed, colour variance between units in a container is expected and is described in the specification we quote against. Buyers who need a tighter range can specify natural-only or multi-colour-only and we will grade to it, at a slightly longer lead time.

name: Mango Wood & Iron Coffee Table
short_description: Solid mango wood top on a powder-coated iron base. Knock-down in two parts, 180–220 pcs in a 40ft HQ, MOQ 50 pcs. Custom sizes and finishes accepted.
long_description: Mango wood is a by-product timber — orchards replant when fruit yield drops, and the felled trees go to furniture instead of firewood. It works easily, takes a natural or lightly stained finish well, and sits at a pale honey colour that suits the industrial look this piece is built for.

The table ships as two parts: a solid top and a powder-coated mild steel base, packed separately. That keeps the container efficient at 180 to 220 pieces in a 40ft HQ and means the base cannot scuff the top in transit. Assembly is four bolts.

This is the easiest piece on our furniture list to customise. Dimensions, top thickness, base geometry and powder-coat colour are all changed at tooling cost of nothing, because the base is fabricated rather than cast. Buyers running their own range usually start here.

name: Hand-Carved Rosewood Bed (King)
short_description: Solid Sheesham with a hand-carved headboard and traditional joinery. Six-part knock-down, 25–30 units in a 40ft HQ, MOQ 10 units, 60–75 day lead time.
long_description: The headboard is carved by hand, which is why the lead time on this piece is 60 to 75 days and why no two are line-for-line identical. Jodhpur and Saharanpur both hold carving workshops where the motifs and the tooling have not changed much in a century, and the depth of relief is what separates this from a machine-routed imitation.

Construction is traditional mortise and tenon at the corners rather than screw-and-dowel. It is slower to build and it is the reason a bed of this weight stays square after years of use. Side rails lock into the posts with steel bed bolts so the frame can be knocked down and reassembled without loosening the joinery.
King is standard at 193 × 203 cm. UK king, US queen and custom sizes are made to order at the same price band, and the carving pattern can be changed to a buyer's drawing on volumes from 20 units.

name: Cane & Rattan Lounge Chair
short_description: Hand-woven natural rattan on a solid wood frame, from Jodhpur and Moradabad. Shipped assembled, 120–150 pcs in a 40ft HQ, MOQ 50 pcs.
long_description: The weave is done by hand on a steam-bent solid wood frame, and the tightness of that weave is what decides whether the chair still holds its shape in three years. Machine-woven cane looks similar in a photograph and goes slack under load; this does not, which is the reason it costs more and the reason it keeps selling.

Jodhpur builds the frames, Moradabad supplies much of the cane work, and the two trades have shipped together for long enough that the joint is not a coordination problem. Natural rattan is the standard finish; black, white and honey stains are available without a lead-time penalty.

Chairs ship assembled because a woven seat cannot be knocked down and rebuilt. Shrink wrap over the weave, then a fitted carton. At 120 to 150 pieces in a 40ft HQ this remains one of the better volume-to-value pieces in the range for a buyer filling a mixed container.
